notes: Single volume, 45 pages / 54 PDF images. Two sitios de ganado mayor (titulo, stamped p14), consistent with the register's 8,780.81 patent acres. Rich back-story visible in the sworn translations, stamped pp.16-19: the land at the Estero Americano was granted to Manuel McIntosh 4 Sept 1839, approved by the Departmental Junta 22 May 1840, with James Dawson and James Black EXCLUDED 'as wanting the indispensable requisite of naturalization to enable them to hold property in Mexican Territory' (stamped p19); Dawson was naturalized at Monterey 27 Dec 1841 by Manuel Jimeno Casarin acting as governor (stamped p17) and petitioned again 18 Sept 1843; he died before the title issued, and Micheltorena granted the Canada de Pogolome to his widow in her own name on 12 Feb 1844. Departmental Assembly approval 26 Sept 1845 (petition, stamped p5). Grant recorded in Sonoma County Book F pp.234-235 on 14 Nov 1851 (endorsement, stamped p15). Board confirmation 11 April 1853; the opinion at transcript p25 was not read, and no patent copy appears in the pages read (register's GLO 51 / 3 Nov 1858 is for Phase C).

notes: Single volume, 42 pages / 48 PDF images. Hoffman's 1862 table carries no year/governor/grantee for this entry (all null in the input), so the case file is the only authority here and it settles every field: three sitios de ganado mayor (titulo condition 3, stamped p12), consistent with the register's 13,316.13 patent acres. Small internal date wrinkle, both 1846: the decree is dated Angeles 26 January 1846 (stamped p10, and the translation at p15) while the titulo issued on it is dated 25 January 1846 (stamped p12); the Assembly committee report (stamped p13) cites 'titulo librado con fha 25 de En.o de este ano', matching the register's 1846 either way. Land was San Diego mission community land declared vacant by the padre ministro Fr. Vicente P. Oliva, 11 Sept 1845 (stamped p9). Juan Lopez abandoned the rancho during the war (Elisalde deposition, stamped p5: 'Lopez left the place on account of the war and of trouble from the Indians'), which is why no judicial possession was ever given (petition, stamped p4). Board confirmation 2 May 1854; the opinion at transcript p25 was not read, and no patent copy appears in the pages read.

notes: Single volume, 76 pages / 89 PDF images. SUBSTANTIVE POINT: there was NO formal titulo here. What the register records as an 1838 Alvarado grant is a marginal decree of PROVISIONAL OCCUPATION pending a report from the administrador of ex-Mission San Francisco de Asis; that report did not come until 30 April 1840 ('Establecimiento de Dolores Abril 30 de 1840. Jose de la C. Sanchez', stamped p15), and on the very same day Jose Maria Alviso ceded his right to his brother by an endorsement on the same sheet ('Cedo mi derecho que por la presente concesion me pertenece a mi Hermano Jose Antonio Alviso ... Sta. Clara Abril 30 de 1840', stamped p15). A cash sale followed at Mission Santa Clara on 2 May 1840 for 1,200 pesos (Exhibit No.1, stamped p18, translated p19), Jose Maria signing with a cross because he could not write. The claimant also produced a separate provisional concession from Jose Castro to Jose Antonio Alviso dated 10 June 1839 (Chaboya deposition, stamped p8). The Board confirmed anyway, 10 July 1855; opinion at transcript p29 not read. Bear in mind for the register's dating: the file's Spanish says 'Mzo. 25 de 1838' (25 March) where the sworn translation says 'April 25th 1838' - the month is contested inside the file, the year is not.

Grant is TEN sitios de ganado mayor (condition 4, stamped transcript p14: 'El terreno de que se hace donacion es de diez sitios de ganado mayor segun esplica el diseno respectivo'), consistent with the register's 44,388.17 patent acres. Useful detail the register does not carry: Josefa Soto petitioned at Monterey 5 Jan 1844 as 'viuda, hija legitima del finado Damasio Soto y M.a Antonia Alviso' and signed at her request by Jorge Allen because she could not write (stamped pp.10-11); Micheltorena referred the expediente to JOHN A. SUTTER as 'encargado del Sacramento', who certified the land vacant at 'Nueva Helvecia Marzo 19 de 1844' over his own signature 'J. A. Sutter, Juzgado del Distrito del Rio Sacramento' (stamped p11); Jimeno then advised suspending all Sacramento and San Joaquin grants pending a gubernatorial visita (stamped p12, 27 March 1844) and Micheltorena concurred, issuing only a provisional occupation permit on 13 July 1844 before finally ordering the title out on 21 Dec 1844 because the visita could not be made and 'estas familias nativas del Departamento y p.r consiguiente mejicanas' were being kept from their farming. Departmental Assembly approval 22 April 1845 under Pio Pico as president and Agustin Olvera as secretary (stamped pp.15-16).
